subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist and next steps
messages:

Subject: Post-demo follow-up + next steps (model priorities)

Thanks again for your time today — great discussion. Short recap + proposed next steps below so we stay aligned: 

Recap:
- Goals: conversational product-support assistant for Acme Cloud with sub-500ms p50 latency, high factual accuracy (priority on correctness for policy answers), and cost target to keep inference spend within your Q4 budget band.
- Data: you confirmed sample logs (~2000 examples) and chat transcripts with priority intents (billing, provisioning, incident triage).
- Constraints: must support multi-turn context up to ~2k tokens, and run in us-west region.

Proposed next steps:
1) We prepare a recommended model shortlist with cost/latency/quality tradeoffs and a suggested prompt set + eval harness (target: 1 week).
2) You share the anonymized sample subset (or we can accept a CSV export) — we can also sign an NDA if preferred.
3) Quick kickoff for technical evals (30–45m) next Wed/Thu.

What we need from you this week:
- Prioritize between latency vs cost vs quality (if you had to pick one).
- Confirm availability for a technical kickoff next Wed/Thu (I proposed two slots in the calendar invite).

Attachments: acme-demo-recording.mp4, redwood-1pager-dedicated.pdf

Thanks — I'll pull together the shortlist once you confirm priorities.


Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — excited to move forward. A few quick answers: 
- Priority: quality first (we need high factual accuracy for customer-facing policy answers), latency second (aim for <500ms p50), cost third but still important.
- Data: we can provide the anonymized sample export by EOD Friday.
- Kickoff: Thu next week (7/8) at 10am PT works for us.

Can you include a shortlist that covers both hosted and dedicated deployment options? We want to understand the tradeoffs if we move to reserved capacity later. Also please include any known regression/quality risks when using quantized variants.

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 5 Jul 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-demo follow-up + shortlist (internal notes)

Internal notes for the shortlist and eval plan (pulling preliminary numbers from internal bench):
- Candidate models to evaluate: 1) OpenLlama-13B (quant 4-bit), 2) RW-13B-v1 (Redwood-verified FP16), 3) Mistral-7B-instruct (int8), 4) Falcon-40B-codex (FP16) as high-quality baseline.
- Latency / cost (approx p50 on A100s):
  - OpenLlama-13B q4: p50 ~ 250–320ms, tokens/sec higher, cost low; risk: instruc-tuning gaps on safety-critical policy answers.
  - RW-13B-v1 fp16: p50 ~ 280–360ms, slightly higher cost than q4 but better out-of-the-box safety/QA profiles (recommended hosted and dedicated candidate).
  - Mistral-7B-int8: p50 ~ 180–240ms, cheapest latency, may struggle on long-context multi-turn completions; good for short clarifications.
  - Falcon-40B fp16: p50 ~ 520–700ms, highest quality on complex reasoning but exceeds target latency (still important as fallback for hard queries).
- Prompt set: curating a 150-example eval set covering Billing, Provisioning, Incident Triage, and Safety/Policy. Attached: acme-eval-promptset-v1.json (anonymized examples).
- Regression risks: quantized variants (q4/int8) may show degradation on policy-specific factual recall and hallucination rate; include control tests in eval harness to measure precision@k on lookup tasks.

I'll prepare a short spreadsheet with tradeoffs and suggested default candidates for hosted vs dedicated.


Neha Kapoor
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acme.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.d@acme.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Jul 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist and next steps

Jordan — thanks for the priority guidance and for committing the sample data. Per our internal bench and Neha's notes, please find our recommended shortlist and rationale below. I attached a concise XLSX (redwood-model-shortlist.xlsx) that summarizes cost, expected p50 latency, and key regression notes.

Recommended shortlist (high-level):
1) RW-13B-v1 (FP16) — Primary recommendation
  - Rationale: Best balance of out-of-the-box safety/QA and predictable latency on our runtime. Meets your quality-first requirement with p50 ~280–360ms on A100-class nodes and can operate in hosted mode today. Lower regression risk than q4 variants.
  - Suggested use: Default for production-facing answers; run with KV-prefix caching for common help articles to lower tail latency/cost.
2) Mistral-7B-instruct (INT8) — Low-latency, cost-efficient candidate
  - Rationale: Strong latency (p50 ~180–240ms) and low cost. Good for clarification turns and short completions; may need prompt engineering for policy recall.
  - Suggested use: Route quick clarification/FAQ intents here to reduce cost while sending higher-risk intents to RW-13B-v1.
3) OpenLlama-13B (Q4) — Cost-optimized option
  - Rationale: Very competitive cost and decent latency, but higher risk on safety/policy recall; consider only for non-sensitive workflows or as a fallback for burst capacity.
4) Falcon-40B (FP16) — High-quality fallback
  - Rationale: Strong on complex reasoning but above latency target; recommend as an async fallback or for rare elevated-importance queries (can be routed with automatic sampling to avoid cost overruns).

Quality regression notes:
- Quantized variants (q4/int8) showed measurable uptick in hallucination on policy lookup tasks in our internal evals — we recommend running a small control set from your anonymized sample to quantify delta.
- We'll surface per-prompt quality deltas in the eval dashboard so you can see which intents degrade the most.

Proposed eval plan (timeline):
- Day 0: Kickoff + access to anonymized sample (you share by EOD Fri).
- Day 1–3: Run parallel evals across the shortlist using the 150-example prompt set (we'll push results to the shared Drive link).
- Day 4: Call to review metrics (accuracy, hallucination rate, latency percentiles, p95/p99), routing recommendations, and final candidate selection.

Links & artifacts: 
- Benchmarks & results folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-acme-benchmarks
- Eval harness + prompt set: https://docs.redwood.ai/evals/acme/2026-07-benchmarks
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/ACME-2026-014

Attachments: acme-eval-promptset-v1.json, redwood-model-shortlist.xlsx

Next steps: please confirm the anonymized sample share and I'll send the calendar invite for Thu 7/8 10am PT (kickoff + we'll walk through the eval harness).

Thanks — looking forward to this.
